label: token right after a k in the original input (t>=2)
explanation: Fires almost only during the original-input phase, on the step right after a k was input (prev_tok=k has 32x lift and about 91% of activation mass). It is mostly early: t=2-3 holds about 79% of mass, and it never fires at t=0/1 or on the delimiter. A few weak activations in the copy phase come at recall_idx=1, right after <DEL>. Only about 4% of post-k steps fire, so precision is low. What decides which ones fire is the rest of the prefix: the rate goes up when the earlier tokens come from {a,b,e,f,g,k,m,o,q,x,w} (first_tok a/e/x/f, prev2_tok a/k/b) and the current token is 1/r/m/t/a/b/k/p. Fitted token sets like these only reach F1 of about 0.5. The strongest examples are short all-letter prefixes such as x a k k b and x e k k p. It does not fire on k itself, after other tokens, or in the copy phase generally.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=k (+5.39), t=2 & prev_tok=k (+4.97), orig0=x (+4.94), orig0=f (+4.83), phase=2 & in_tok=x (+4.55), prev2_tok=k (+4.33). Lower it: prev2_tok=x (-4.99), prev2_tok=f (-4.45), in_tok=j (-3.31), orig_idx=-1 (-3.24).
